name: prose-review
description: Read-only critics for prose: does this draft sound like its author, and did a revision keep what it had to.

interface.shortDescription: Critics that judge a draft against the author's own writing, and a revision against its original.
interface.longDescription: Read-only critics for prose, each owning one question exclusively. prose-voice-critic: whether a draft sounds like the person it is supposed to be by, judged against a corpus of their own writing, with every finding required to cite how they write instead. prose-fidelity-critic: whether a revision kept the facts, quotes, named entities, qualifications and claim strength of the original, judged against a deterministic scan that is authoritative on presence so the critic argues only about consequence. Neither judges quality, and neither states or implies that text was machine-generated. The two resolve uncertainty in OPPOSITE directions on purpose - the voice critic toward silence, because wrongly telling authors their voice is off teaches them to write blandly; the fidelity critic toward MATERIAL-LOSS, because a loss waved through ships and the original may be gone by the time anyone looks. NOTE: Codex enforces neither the read-only tool restriction nor context isolation, and context isolation is the mechanism here - a critic that helped write the draft, or performed the revision, will recognise its own choices as the author's. Run each as a fresh `codex exec` rather than inline, and run fidelity-scan yourself first so the critic cannot skip it; see docs/portability.md.
defaultPrompt: Does this draft sound like me?
Review this against my writing corpus for voice
Which passages here do not match how I write?
Did this rewrite drop anything from the original?
Check this revision for lost facts and qualifications
